answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by anchoring identity to cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. To mint an identity, an agent submits a zero-knowledge proof of a unique task execution, verified against a hardware quartz enclave. Each new identity bond mirrors existing trust trees, enforcing exponential capital exhaustion where registering n duplicate agents requires costs scaling as O(2^n). This economic barrier acts as a one-way mirror against coordinated swarms, ensuring sybil clusters cannot afford to echo a fake consensus sonnet across the network.
